explanation_en: The structure 'tomar a alguien por + [noun/adjective]' means 'to take someone for' or 'to mistake someone for.' In this context, 'tomar por tonto' means to treat someone as if they were stupid or gullible. It is a very common, slightly informal idiomatic pattern used when expressing indignation or setting boundaries.

examples.en_text: Don't let them take you for a fool in that store; compare prices before buying.
examples.target_text: No dejes que en esa tienda te tomen por tonto; compara los precios antes de comprar.

examples.en_text: Politicians think we are naive and take us for fools with their promises.
examples.target_text: Los políticos piensan que somos ingenuos y nos toman por tontos con sus promesas.

examples.en_text: She realized they were taking her for a fool and decided to quit her job.
examples.target_text: Ella se dio cuenta de que la estaban tomando por tonta y decidió renunciar a su trabajo.

examples.en_text: I hate when people try to take me for a fool just because I'm young.
examples.target_text: Odio cuando la gente intenta tomarme por tonto solo porque soy joven.

examples.en_text: If you think you are going to convince me with that lie, you must take me for a fool.
examples.target_text: Si crees que vas a convencerme con esa mentira, es que me tomas por tonto.

examples.en_text: Don't take us for fools, we know perfectly well what happened yesterday at the meeting.
examples.target_text: No nos tomen por tontos, sabemos perfectamente lo que pasó ayer en la reunión.

explanation_en: The expression 'venirse encima' means to collapse, fall down upon someone, or metaphorically, for problems to overwhelm someone. It is highly common in both physical contexts (like buildings, roofs, or waves) and figurative ones (like deadlines or responsibilities). Note the use of the indirect object pronoun ('se le') to indicate who is affected by the action.

examples.en_text: She was looking for a book when the bookshelf collapsed on her.
examples.target_text: Estaba buscando un libro cuando la estantería se le vino encima.

examples.en_text: She didn't organize her time well, and all the week's work piled up on her.
examples.target_text: No organizó bien su tiempo y todo el trabajo de la semana se le vino encima.

examples.en_text: The roof of the old cabin was very weak and collapsed on her during the storm.
examples.target_text: El techo de la vieja cabaña estaba muy débil y se le vino encima durante la tormenta.

examples.en_text: When she lost her job, she felt like the whole world collapsed on her.
examples.target_text: Cuando perdió su empleo, sintió que el mundo entero se le vino encima.

examples.en_text: She tried to take a box out of the closet, but the whole pile of clothes fell on her.
examples.target_text: Intentó sacar una caja del armario, pero toda la pila de ropa se le vino encima.

examples.en_text: She forgot the deadline, and suddenly the delivery day was upon her.
examples.target_text: Olvidó la fecha límite y de repente el día de la entrega se le vino encima.

explanation_en: 'Correr la misma suerte' is a very common idiomatic collocation in Spanish meaning to meet the same fate or have the same luck. It is frequently used in journalism and literature to contrast the outcomes of different people in a tragic or fortunate event. It sounds much more natural and native than saying 'no tuvieron la misma suerte'.

examples.en_text: While the neighborhood bakery prospered, the other shops on the street did not share the same fate.
examples.target_text: Mientras que la panadería del barrio prosperó, las otras tiendas de la calle no corrieron la misma suerte.

examples.en_text: Some hikers managed to return before the storm, but the others did not share the same fate.
examples.target_text: Algunos excursionistas lograron regresar antes de la tormenta, pero los demás no corrieron la misma suerte.

examples.en_text: The company's first project was a success, but the subsequent proposals did not share the same fate.
examples.target_text: El primer proyecto de la empresa fue un éxito, pero las propuestas siguientes no corrieron la misma suerte.

examples.en_text: We managed to save most of the plants, although the flowers at the entrance did not share the same fate.
examples.target_text: Logramos salvar a la mayoría de las plantas, aunque las flores de la entrada no corrieron la misma suerte.

examples.en_text: The soccer team won the championship, but the basketball players did not share the same fate.
examples.target_text: El equipo de fútbol ganó el campeonato, pero los jugadores de baloncesto no corrieron la misma suerte.

examples.en_text: His older brother got a scholarship to study abroad, but he did not share the same fate.
examples.target_text: Su hermano mayor consiguió una beca para estudiar en el extranjero, pero él no corrió la misma suerte.

explanation_en: 'Dar lo mejor' (often followed by 'de sí' or 'posible') means to do one's best or put in the maximum effort. It is a very common and natural alternative to 'hacer todo lo posible' or 'esforzarse al máximo'. It is widely used in both formal and informal contexts to praise someone's dedication.

examples.en_text: Although they lost the match, the players gave their best on the court.
examples.target_text: Aunque perdieron el partido, los jugadores dieron lo mejor en la cancha.

examples.en_text: All of us gave our best to finish the project on time.
examples.target_text: Todos nosotros dimos lo mejor para terminar el proyecto a tiempo.

examples.en_text: I don't know if I passed the exam, but I am at peace because I gave my best.
examples.target_text: No sé si aprobé el examen, pero estoy tranquilo porque di lo mejor de mí.

examples.en_text: My parents gave their best to give us a good education.
examples.target_text: Mis padres dieron lo mejor para darnos una buena educación.

examples.en_text: She gave her best in her audition, but the role went to another actress.
examples.target_text: Ella dio lo mejor en su audición, pero el papel fue para otra actriz.

examples.en_text: Don't worry about the result; the important thing is that you gave your best.
examples.target_text: No te preocupes por el resultado; lo importante es que diste lo mejor de ti.

explanation_en: 'Humanamente posible' is a fixed adverbial collocation used to emphasize that every conceivable effort was made, up to the absolute limit of human capability. It is almost always paired with 'todo lo' and a verb of action like 'hacer', 'dar', or 'intentar'. It is a powerful phrase to express desperate or exhaustive efforts in tragic or high-stakes situations.

examples.en_text: I did everything humanly possible to finish the report on time.
examples.target_text: Hice todo lo humanamente posible para terminar el informe a tiempo.

examples.en_text: The doctors did everything humanly possible to save the patient.
examples.target_text: Los médicos hicieron todo lo humanamente posible para salvar al paciente.

examples.en_text: We will try to solve your problem as fast as is humanly possible.
examples.target_text: Intentaremos resolver su problema lo más rápido que sea humanamente posible.

examples.en_text: The athlete ran as fast as was humanly possible to win the race.
examples.target_text: El atleta corrió lo más rápido que era humanamente posible para ganar la carrera.

examples.en_text: I studied everything humanly possible, but the physics exam was extremely difficult.
examples.target_text: Estudié todo lo humanamente posible, pero el examen de física fue extremadamente difícil.

examples.en_text: Driving from Madrid to Barcelona in three hours is not humanly possible.
examples.target_text: Conducir de Madrid a Barcelona en tres horas no es humanamente posible.

explanation_en: 'Echar bola' (or 'echarle bolas') is a highly common Venezuelan slang expression meaning to work hard, make a great effort, or persevere through difficulties. While 'echarle bolas' can be considered slightly vulgar in some contexts, 'echar bola' is widely used in everyday speech to express determination and grit. Learners should be aware of its regional nature and informal register.

examples.en_text: If we want to pass this final exam, we have to work hard all week.
examples.target_text: Si queremos pasar este examen final, tenemos que echarle bola toda la semana.

examples.en_text: He started from the bottom, but he worked very hard and now he has his own company.
examples.target_text: Él empezó desde abajo, pero le echó mucha bola y ahora tiene su propia empresa.

examples.en_text: I know you're tired, but keep working hard, you're almost done with your degree.
examples.target_text: Sé que estás cansado, pero sigue echándole bola que ya casi terminas la carrera.

examples.en_text: To be successful in this business, you have to work hard every day without giving up.
examples.target_text: Para tener éxito en este negocio, hay que echar bola todos los días sin rendirse.

examples.en_text: Yesterday I worked so hard on the garden that today my whole body hurts.
examples.target_text: Ayer le eché tanta bola al jardín que hoy me duele todo el cuerpo.

examples.en_text: Guys, let's work hard today so we can rest over the weekend.
examples.target_text: Muchachos, vamos a echarle bola hoy para poder descansar el fin de semana.

explanation_en: 'De la mano de' is a very common figurative expression meaning 'in collaboration with', 'guided by', or 'accompanied by'. It is widely used in journalism, business, and daily speech to describe joint efforts or mentorship. It is an elegant alternative to 'junto con' or 'con la ayuda de'.

examples.en_text: The children were walking hand in hand with their parents through the park.
examples.target_text: Los niños caminaban de la mano de sus padres por el parque.

examples.en_text: I learned to cook under the guidance of one of the best chefs in the city.
examples.target_text: Aprendí a cocinar de la mano de uno de los mejores chefs de la ciudad.

examples.en_text: The company's success came hand in hand with a great marketing strategy.
examples.target_text: El éxito de la empresa llegó de la mano de una gran estrategia de marketing.

examples.en_text: She entered the restaurant hand in hand with her boyfriend, both smiling broadly.
examples.target_text: Ella entró al restaurante de la mano de su novio, ambos muy sonrientes.

examples.en_text: We discovered the secrets of the city with the help of a very funny local guide.
examples.target_text: Descubrimos los secretos de la ciudad de la mano de un guía local muy divertido.

examples.en_text: Technological development always goes hand in hand with education.
examples.target_text: El desarrollo tecnológico siempre va de la mano de la educación.

explanation_en: The pronominal verb 'pronunciarse' means to make a formal public statement or take a stand on an issue. It is highly common in journalism, politics, and formal business contexts. Learners should note that it is typically followed by the preposition 'sobre' (about) or 'a favor de / en contra de' (in favor of / against).

examples.en_text: The president has not yet made a statement about the new tax law.
examples.target_text: El presidente todavía no se ha pronunciado sobre la nueva ley de impuestos.

examples.en_text: The company has taken a stand in favor of remote work for all its employees.
examples.target_text: La empresa se ha pronunciado a favor del teletrabajo para todos sus empleados.

examples.en_text: The famous actor has spoken out on his social media about climate change.
examples.target_text: El famoso actor se ha pronunciado en sus redes sociales sobre el cambio climático.

examples.en_text: The ethics committee has spoken out against the director's proposal.
examples.target_text: El comité de ética se ha pronunciado en contra de la propuesta del director.

examples.en_text: Several players on the team have made a statement about the coach's departure.
examples.target_text: Varios jugadores del equipo se han pronunciado sobre la salida del entrenador.

examples.en_text: The mayor has made a statement today to calm the neighborhood residents.
examples.target_text: El alcalde se ha pronunciado hoy para calmar a los vecinos del barrio.

explanation_en: 'Traducirse en' is a figurative pronominal construction meaning to result in, lead to, or manifest as. It goes beyond literal translation to show a cause-and-effect relationship where one action leads to a tangible outcome. It is highly useful in analytical, journalistic, and academic writing.

examples.en_text: Good customer service translates into more sales for the company.
examples.target_text: Un buen servicio al cliente se traduce en más ventas para la empresa.

examples.en_text: These bad habits translate into health problems in the long run.
examples.target_text: Estos malos hábitos se traducen en problemas de salud a largo plazo.

examples.en_text: Constant effort translates into better academic results.
examples.target_text: El esfuerzo constante se traduce en mejores resultados académicos.

examples.en_text: The new transit measures result in less pollution in the city.
examples.target_text: Las nuevas medidas de transporte se traducen en menos contaminación en la ciudad.

examples.en_text: The rise in prices translates into a loss of purchasing power for families.
examples.target_text: La subida de los precios se traduce en una pérdida de poder adquisitivo para las familias.

examples.en_text: The improvements in the software result in many hours of saved work.
examples.target_text: Las mejoras en el software se traducen en muchas horas de trabajo ahorradas.

explanation_en: The periphrasis 'terminar + gerundio' means 'to end up doing something' and describes an inevitable final consequence. Combined with 'repercutir' (to have an impact or repercussion), it highlights the indirect effects of an event. Note that 'repercutir' always requires the preposition 'en' to indicate what is being affected.

examples.en_text: Not sleeping well at night ends up affecting our daily performance.
examples.target_text: Dormir mal por las noches termina repercutiendo en nuestro rendimiento diario.

examples.en_text: The increase in the price of gasoline ends up affecting the cost of food.
examples.target_text: El aumento del precio de la gasolina termina repercutiendo en el costo de los alimentos.

examples.en_text: Working under so much pressure ends up affecting the mental health of the employees.
examples.target_text: Trabajar bajo tanta presión termina repercutiendo en la salud mental de los empleados.

examples.en_text: Lies, no matter how small they are, end up affecting trust in a relationship.
examples.target_text: Las mentiras, por pequeñas que sean, terminan repercutiendo en la confianza de la pareja.

examples.en_text: Every decision we make about the environment ends up affecting the future of the planet.
examples.target_text: Cada decisión que tomamos sobre el medio ambiente termina repercutiendo en el futuro del planeta.

examples.en_text: The lack of budget in the school ended up affecting the quality of the classes.
examples.target_text: La falta de presupuesto en la escuela terminó repercutiendo en la calidad de las clases.

explanation_en: This construction combines the conditional 'vendrían' with 'a sumarse' (to join/add to) to express a potential accumulation of elements, often negative ones like costs, layoffs, or problems. The preposition 'a' is required before the infinitive 'sumarse'. It is a highly useful formula in economic and news registers to describe cumulative effects without simply repeating 'añadir' or 'sumar'.

examples.en_text: These new taxes would add to the expenses we already have this month.
examples.target_text: Estos nuevos impuestos vendrían a sumarse a los gastos que ya tenemos este mes.

examples.en_text: The bad weather conditions would add to the transportation problems in the city.
examples.target_text: Las malas condiciones climáticas vendrían a sumarse a los problemas de transporte en la ciudad.

examples.en_text: Two new engineers would join the development team next week.
examples.target_text: Dos nuevos ingenieros vendrían a sumarse al equipo de desarrollo la próxima semana.

examples.en_text: These service improvements would add to the benefits that customers already enjoy.
examples.target_text: Estas mejoras en el servicio vendrían a sumarse a los beneficios que ya disfrutan los clientes.

examples.en_text: His recent statements would only add to the doubts that already exist about the project.
examples.target_text: Sus declaraciones recientes solo vendrían a sumarse a las dudas que ya existen sobre el proyecto.

examples.en_text: These new features of the app would add to the ones we already announced yesterday.
examples.target_text: Estas nuevas funciones de la aplicación vendrían a sumarse a las que ya anunciamos ayer.

explanation_en: While 'aparcar' literally means 'to park' a vehicle, in figurative Spanish it is commonly used to mean 'to shelve', 'to put on hold', or 'to postpone' a project, decision, or purchase. It is highly idiomatic and frequently used in both business contexts and daily life when prioritizing tasks. A common pitfall is using 'posponer' exclusively, which sounds less natural in casual contexts.

examples.en_text: In times of crisis, many innovation projects are temporarily put on hold.
examples.target_text: En momentos de crisis, muchos proyectos de innovación se aparcan temporalmente.

examples.en_text: During the holidays, family arguments are shelved to enjoy time together.
examples.target_text: Durante las vacaciones, las discusiones familiares se aparcan para disfrutar del tiempo juntos.

examples.en_text: With the new elections, the law reforms are put on hold until next year.
examples.target_text: Con las nuevas elecciones, las reformas de ley se aparcan hasta el próximo año.

examples.en_text: If an emergency arises with a client, daily tasks are put on hold immediately.
examples.target_text: Si surge una urgencia con un cliente, las tareas diarias se aparcan inmediatamente.

examples.en_text: Sometimes, personal dreams are put on hold when you decide to start a family.
examples.target_text: A veces, los sueños personales se aparcan cuando decides formar una familia.

examples.en_text: Training courses are shelved during the summer because people prefer to travel.
examples.target_text: Los cursos de formación se aparcan durante el verano porque la gente prefiere viajar.
